questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country to improve my language skills. A multicultural city with a lot of opportunities. Liverpool was recommended by one of my friends who studied here during Covid.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my time in Liverpool with an amazing group of international friends Highly recommend it!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was good! I got the information I needed by asking the staff at LJMU.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The teachers/tutors were very helpful and welcoming, although I wish LJMU had planned an introduction day/week to get to know the other students and meet other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had the opportunity to choose between two different student accommodations through LJMU of which I chose Marybone because my friend recommended the area. I'm very satisfied with my student accommodation and the friendly staff here.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living with strangers in student accommodation is a great way of building a social life.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was okay, but confusing to figure out what courses I could attend and match courses outside the screen school program.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I emailed the staff and they were very friendly and helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study Graphic Design and Illustration which isn't in the screen school program, but I was allowed to attend.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in other courses than the given ones, it does not hurt to ask.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were completely different from any course I have had at UCPH as they were creative courses, which meant that I had to adjust to a new learning environment, way of thinking and studying. It was hard in the beginning, but eventually, I got used to it. Overall, I think the workload was lower than at UCPH but at the same time, it is hard to compare as I did not have to read and write academic papers, but rather produce creative outcomes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures were quite similar to lectures at UCPH. We had tutorials where every student had a one to one chat with a tutor for guidance on the projects, which was very helpful.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Images, Words and Discourse

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed studying these courses but I also found it difficult to teach myself how to use create cloud programs like Photoshop, fortunately, the two guys in the digital images studio could help with anything, so it was not a problem after discovering the digital image studio.

questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I knew that it would be cheaper to live in Liverpool than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not attempt anything arranged by the university as I am not sure they arranged anything for exchange students other than the meet up we had in the beginning. I got friends where I lived so I did not look into activities arranged by LJMU.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The company Daytripper arranged some fantastic day trips to other places in the UK - highly recommend the trips to Wales.

These trips were very convenient as we just had to book a ticket and then we got on and off the bus in Liverpool.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Other cities in England. The beautiful nature in Wales. Musicals. Picnics in the parks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as I really love exploring new cultures and meeting people!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I only socialized with other international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly and helpful everyone is in Liverpool.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy the time - it flies so fast.

2. Use a lot of time and energy in the beginning on socialising and making friends.

3. It is very nice to have one familiar face in the same city. One of my close friends also studied in Liverpool but at another university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to the tutors about any concerns, they are listening and taking it into account.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the memories I have with my international friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the new teaching environment and way of thinking.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just go!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
